instructions: Footprint geo/growth/editorial slots. Owner-facing voice only.

rows.body: Radisson Blu under Choice Hotels is an upper-upscale flag with a strong Caribbean and Latin America presence—open hotels in Argentina (Bariloche), Brazil (Belo Horizonte Savassi, São Paulo), Chile (Santiago), and Aruba—alongside select U.S. and Canada properties. When you evaluate this flag, plan for Inspired Professional guests, Nordic Nouveau capital requirements, and Choice Privileges economics—not core Radisson conversion assumptions.

rows.title: Americas
rows.body:
Selective Americas scale

U.S. and Canada hotels help guests recognize the brand in domestic gateway markets. For Caribbean and Latin America projects, compare your asset to open Blu hotels in São Paulo, Santiago, Belo Horizonte Savassi, Bariloche, and Aruba—they show how the flag competes in upper-upscale urban and resort markets. Confirm hotel counts and pipeline in your franchise disclosure.

rows.title: CALA
rows.body:
Strong CALA relevance

Open Choice-affiliated Radisson Blu hotels in Brazil, Chile, Argentina, and Aruba reflect upper-upscale urban and resort positioning—design-forward public spaces and full-service scope rather than light Radisson conversion economics.

rows.title: Europe
rows.body:
Global heritage

Most global Blu history and design standards come from Europe. If your deal is in the Americas, you may still reference European standards for FF&E and brand identity—confirm what applies to your agreement and market.

rows.title: MEA
rows.body:
Selective relevance

Middle East and Africa exposure varies by country and operator. For Americas projects, base your footprint assumptions on CALA and U.S. disclosure—not MEA ramp curves. Confirm counts in your FDD.

rows.title: APAC
rows.body:
Gateway relevance

International travelers may know Blu from Asia-Pacific and European gateways. For U.S. or CALA franchise deals, focus on hotels in your region unless the asset is located in APAC.

CALA urban gateway upper-upscale
Resort and leisure destinations (Aruba, Bariloche)
Design-forward conversion and adaptive reuse
Meetings-capable metro hotels (São Paulo, Santiago)
Secondary-city upper-upscale (Belo Horizonte Savassi)
Markets with strong corporate and leisure compression

Radisson Blu fits when you need recognizable upper-upscale design, memorable public spaces, and Choice distribution—not a soft brand with unclear standards. Open CALA hotels can help you judge positioning; your hotel’s returns still depend on market, prototype, fees, and operator execution.

Top urban and resort CALA destinations
Sponsors who can fund upper-upscale FF&E and F&B
Meetings and group product where the prototype supports it
Operators with full-service and design-forward experience
Markets where core Radisson economics understate the asset’s potential

Radisson Blu under Choice is a global upper-upscale flag with momentum in the Americas: Nordic Nouveau design, selective U.S. and Canada hotels, and growing CALA openings. It works best when guests expect distinctive design and service—and when you can fund casegoods and public-space investment beyond a logo change.

Reference CALA hotels: Bariloche, São Paulo, Belo Horizonte Savassi, Plaza El Bosque Santiago, Aruba
Upper-upscale urban and resort—not core Radisson beach or airport conversion plays
Global Radisson Hotel Group scale supports recognition; Choice-affiliated Americas count is smaller
Strongest fit when corporate/leisure demand and FF&E budget match upper-upscale standards
